design_gotchas.title: Razor-Thin 0.5 V Supply Margin (16.5 V Abs Max vs 16 V Rec Max) — Unsafe on ±8 V Ripple or 24 V Rails
design_gotchas.detail: Section 7.1 (p.8) and Section 10 CAUTION (p.27) cap VDD Abs Max at strictly 16.5 V—only 0.5 V above the 16 V operating ceiling! Even ±5% tolerance on a 16 V rail or inductive transients on ±8 V split supplies exceed 16.5 V, and swapping TLV2372IDR into 24 V/30 V LM358DR or ±15 V TL072IDR sockets causes instant destruction.

design_gotchas.title: Tight -0.2 V to VDD + 0.2 V Input Abs Max Clamp Limit (Earlier Fault Conduction Than Standard ±0.3 V)
design_gotchas.detail: Input voltage Abs Max is -0.2 V to VDD + 0.2 V (with ±10 mA max input current, p.8)—tighter than the typical ±0.3 V–0.5 V spec on most CMOS op-amps. Add series current-limiting resistors whenever sensor signals can arrive before VDD powers up or swing slightly below GND.

design_gotchas.title: Weak Output Drive (4–8 mA at 2.7–5 V) & Rail-to-Rail Crossover CMRR Drop (55 dB Min @ 5 V)
design_gotchas.detail: At VO = 0.5 V from either rail, TLV2372IDR delivers only 4–5 mA at 2.7 V and 7–8 mA at 5 V (p.12), so heavy loads (<1 kOhm) rapidly collapse output swing. Furthermore, full rail-to-rail input operation crosses the NMOS/PMOS transition near VDD - 1.35 V, dropping CMRR from 80 dB down to 72 dB typ / 55 dB min (54 dB over temp, p.11) and raising 15 V open-loop gain loss (AVD drops to 83 dB typ / 79 dB min at 15 V).

design_gotchas.title: No Shutdown Pin on TLV2372 (Only TLV2370/2373/2375) & 4.5–6.0 mV Offset Limits Precision DC
design_gotchas.detail: Although the datasheet title advertises 'With Shutdown,' the 8-pin dual TLV2372IDR has NO shutdown pin (shutdown exists only on 10/14-pin TLV2373 and 6-pin TLV2370, Table 2 p.3). With 4.5 mV max VOS @ 25°C (6 mV over temp) and 39 nV/rtHz noise, step up to OPA2333AIDR or OPA2197IDR for precision low-offset loops.

typical_use_cases: Single-supply 2.7 V to 15 V (±1.35 V to ±7.5 V) high-impedance pA-bias CMOS sensor interfaces and portable blood-glucose/medical meters
Pin-compatible RRIO upgrade over LM358DR / LMV358IDR on 3.3 V–15 V rails where ground-to-VDD input/output swing and 3 MHz / 2.4 V/us speed are required
Extended industrial (-40°C to +125°C) 12 V active filters, white goods, and remote battery-powered telemetry buffers
engineering_summary: The Texas Instruments TLV2372IDR is a 2.7 V to 16 V (±1.35 V to ±8 V), 3 MHz GBWP, 2.4 V/us rail-to-rail input and output (RRIO) dual CMOS operational amplifier in an 8-pin SOIC (D) package rated from -40°C to +125°C (RθJA = 138.4 °C/W). Featuring 1 pA typ input bias current at 550 uA/ch (5 V; 750 uA/ch at 15 V), it bridges the gap between 5.5 V RRIO amps (TLV9002/LMV358) and higher-voltage 12 V–15 V industrial rails on the standard dual SOIC-8 pinout—but engineers must guard its razor-thin 16.5 V abs max supply rating, tight ±0.2 V input rail clamps, modest 7–8 mA (5 V) output drive, and 4.5 mV max offset.
